doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27

title: Humpback Daly and Bill Gallaty, great trombonists
summary: Laine rates Humpback Daly and Bill Gallaty as the best trombonists, noting Gallaty's son plays trumpet.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: This is one of the finest trombone players I ever heard. You're wrong. Yeah. You're wrong. Who's the finest? Uh, Humpback Daly, they could give them all chords and spades and beat them out. Yeah. Really? I never heard him. Jesus Christ, Humpback Daly. Oh, he was good.
Val or Slide, either. Val or Slide. Yeah, he was good.
He was good. He was good.

Give them all chords and spades and beat them out. Yeah. And Perkins was a trombone player but Perkins couldn't hold a trombone player alongside Humpback Gallaty, Bill Gallaty. Bill Gallaty. Oh, that's the father of the present trumpet player.
Bill Gallaty. He's playing trumpet, his son?
He played the mount harp too, don't he? His son. I never knew that, didn't he? I'm his godfather. Yeah? Yeah.
Well, the old man was a fine trombone player. Oh!
